paper.title: Regret Minimization in Bilateral Trade With Perturbed Markets

settings.name_in_paper: Online bilateral trade in perturbed markets, distributional benchmark OPT^D, sigma-smooth unperturbed distribution
unmapped: Bilateral trade: learner posts price pair (p,q) in [0,1]^2 to seller and buyer; reward is gain from trade
One-bit feedback: only whether the trade occurred is observed
Global budget balance constraint: cumulative revenue must be non-negative almost surely
Corruption C defined as sum_t TV(L_t, P) between per-round valuation distribution and an unperturbed distribution P
Unperturbed distribution P is sigma-smooth (sigma treated as constant)
Benchmark is best distribution over price pairs that is budget balanced in expectation
settings.definition_quote: The environment is characterized by a probability distribution $\cP$ ... there is a perturbation parameter $C$, which is defined as the cumulative total variation distance ... $C \coloneq \sum_{t=1}^T  \lVert \cL_t - \mathcal{P} \rVert_{\textnormal{TV}}.$ ... we assume the unperturbed distribution $\cP$ to be $\sigma$-smoothed

settings.name_in_paper: Online bilateral trade, fixed-price benchmark OPT^F, oblivious adversary
unmapped: Bilateral trade with one-bit feedback; valuations in [0,1]^2 drawn from distributions L_t chosen by an oblivious adversary
Global budget balance constraint on learner
settings.definition_quote: These valuations are realizations of a joint time-dependent probability distribution $\mathcal{L}_t$ with support in $[0,1]^2$, chosen by an oblivious adversary. ... $\opt^{\,\textnormal{F}} := \max_{p \in [0, 1]} \sum_{t=1}^T \gft_t(p, p)$

conditions: unperturbed distribution P is sigma-smooth, sigma treated as constant
algorithm is GBB (cumulative revenue non-negative a.s.)

source.label: theo: main
source.quote: There exists a GBB algorithm that, with probability $1-\cO(1/T)$,  guarantees: \[ \sum_{t=1}^T \gft_t(p_t,q_t)\ge \max\{ \opt^{\,\textnormal{D}}- O(C\log(T)), \opt^{\,\textnormal{F}}  \} - \tilde \cO(T^{3/4}) . \]

results.notes: Regret against the best distribution over price pairs that is budget balanced in expectation (comparator is a fixed randomized policy). Bound is O~(T^{3/4}) + O(C log T); probability 1-O(1/T).

source.label: theo: main
source.quote: There exists a GBB algorithm that, with probability $1-\cO(1/T)$,  guarantees: \[ \sum_{t=1}^T \gft_t(p_t,q_t)\ge \max\{ \opt^{\,\textnormal{D}}- O(C\log(T)), \opt^{\,\textnormal{F}}  \} - \tilde \cO(T^{3/4}) . \]

results.notes: Fixed-price benchmark part of Theorem 2; holds without sigma-smoothness and for any C in [0,T].
